answer: Because the sparrow ledger attributes every share, the garden audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 71% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, which means it pays the ocean fee twice and still divides one payout. That is 24 dollars per alias. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
